newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: KHD launches power project in Sri Lanka.
newsitem.headline: KHD launches power project in Sri Lanka.

text.p: KHD Great Britain, a unit of Germany's Kloeckner-Humboldt-Deutz AG began construction of a 51-megawatt power plant in a suburb of the Sri Lankan capital on Friday, a company official said.
"The project was inaugurated today. It plans to generate power by about August of next year," said the official.
The $62 million diesel-powered plant, to function on a build, own and operate (BOO) basis, will add aproximately 16.5 percent more power to the Indian Ocean island's grid, he said.
The plant's entire output will be purchased by the state power utility Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB), he added.
Sri Lanka has several such small power plants in the pipeline to reduce its current dependence on hydroelectricity after suffering from drought for two years in a row.
Sri Lanka's dependence on hydropower is expected to be slashed to 70 percent from the current 83 percent by next month when a 115-megawatt gas turbine and a 40-megawatt diesel plant are commissioned.
The CEB says it plans to further reduce hydropower to 57 percent of total capacity by building more thermal power plants.
The CEB also has plans to construct a 300-megawatt coal-fired power plant in the island's northwest, to be commissioned by the year 2000.
Sri Lanka now has a permanent installed capacity of 1,135 megawatts of hydroelectric power and 250 megawatts of thermal power.
